summary.headline: Star Cement Q1 FY27 EBITDA fell to INR203 crore (INR1,497/t) from INR230 crore, with PAT at INR74 crore versus INR98 crore on subsidy cuts and fuel costs.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue rose to about INR902 crore from INR847 crore, but EBITDA declined to INR203 crore and EBITDA per tonne dropped to INR1,497 from INR1,774. Management attributed the fall to lower Assam incentive accruals (GST cut from 28% to 18%), higher packing and fuel costs, and a kiln shutdown. Cement volumes grew about 7% to 13.02 lakh tonnes, but Northeast volume was flat, and management cut FY27 cement volume growth guidance to 8-9% from 11-12%. Management also updated the Rajasthan (Nimbol) and Haryana (Jhajjar) expansion plan, with capex now about INR2,700 crore (INR2,900 crore incl. GST).

segments.name: Northeast cement
segments.commentary: Sold about 8.71 lakh tonnes vs 8.67 lakh tonnes YoY, essentially flat; management attributed the weakness to April Assam elections and monsoon, not competition.

segments.name: Outside Northeast (Bihar, West Bengal)
segments.commentary: Sold 4.31 lakh tonnes vs 3.55 lakh tonnes YoY (up ~21%), the main volume growth driver this quarter.

segments.name: Building Solutions (AAC, RMC)
segments.commentary: Management said the INR150 crore revenue target is a revenue (not EBITDA) estimate; current run-rate is below it, with ARR expected to reach that level by Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 cement volume growth revised to 8-9% from 11-12%; Northeast growth target 8-9% vs industry about 7%.
FY27 clinker sales expected flat to down 5-10% vs FY26 as clinker is now sourced externally in the Northeast.
Q2 FY27 EBITDA per tonne guided at about INR1,400, with INR1,500-1,600 for the full year.
Fuel cost guided to fall from INR1.55/kcal-equivalent in Q1 to about INR1.45 in Q2 and lower in Q3-Q4 (CFO/MD cited Q4 FY26 at INR1.33).
Assam incentive for FY27 revised to about INR115 crore from earlier INR145 crore due to new equated payout rules.

Cost savings of INR60-70 crore expected in Q2 vs Q1 from lower one-off donation and incentive items; further savings from Silchar railway siding (Oct-Nov), Siliguri wagon tippler (about INR150/t saving on Siliguri sales), and EVs over 5-6 months.
Expects double-digit volume growth in Q3-Q4 FY27 once flood waters recede, with pent-up demand.
Subsidy drag expected to end after September 2026, as GST cut base effect rolls off.
capex_capacity: Rajasthan (Nimbol) integrated plant: 3.0 million tonnes grinding and 3.3 million tonnes clinker; public hearing in August, EC expected by early October, groundwork from mid-October to November; commissioning in about 18-20 months (Q4 FY28 to Q1 FY29).
Jhajjar (Haryana) plant of 2 million tonnes; total expansion capex about INR2,700 crore (about INR2,900 crore including GST), vs earlier INR2,250 crore Nimbol plus about INR650 crore Haryana.
Q1 FY27 capex spend about INR93 crore; FY27 capex guidance of INR500 crore unchanged; FY28 capex about INR1,500 crore.

West Bengal grinding decision pending the state industrial policy (expected around 15 August): may redirect the 2 million tonne Bihar (Begusarai) grinding capex to a Siliguri brownfield unit, though a single 1 million tonne unit may not be economic.
Rajasthan plant has standard state package (capital subsidy plus SGST); quantum to be disclosed on a slide.
Northeast clinker capacity about 15.5-16 million tonnes and grinding about 23-24 million tonnes; about 1 million tonnes each of clinker and grinding expected from two players over the next 3 years.
demand_pricing: Northeast demand muted in Q1 and Q2 due to elections, then flooding in Assam; July volumes fell about 12% YoY and August shows marginal growth.
Prices broadly flat since Q1; up about INR3/bag in Northeast and West Bengal and about INR10 in Bihar, with no cuts despite demand weakness.
Packing (PP bag) costs up due to international war-driven crude price increase; management said these are hard to predict.
Premium (PPC/OPC) share about 15.9%; trade share about 80%; lead distance about 210 km; clinker factor about 66.5%; green share about 3% including WHRS.
Fuel mix Q1: FSA about 45%, spot coal about 30%, balance biomass and others; coal diverted to power plants limited FSA rake availability.
Sand mining crackdown in West Bengal has weighed on regional cement demand.
Management said Sept 2025 base was weak due to GST cut, so September 2026 should show easier comparison.

qa_highlights.question: Will volume growth improve in Q2 and what is FY27 volume outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 volume growth is limited by Assam floods; management now expects FY27 cement growth of 8-9% vs earlier 11-12%, with double-digit growth in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Is INR1,500/t EBITDA sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes over the full year (INR1,500-1,600/t), but Q2 is guided to about INR1,400/t due to shutdown costs and rain-hit fixed-cost absorption.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rajasthan timeline and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: EC expected by October, construction from November, commissioning in 18-20 months; combined Rajasthan and Haryana capex about INR2,700 crore (INR2,900 crore with GST).

qa_highlights.question: Is a QIP planned and what leverage is targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: No active QIP plan; management targets about 1.5-1.6x net debt/EBITDA to fund expansion, with QIP considered only for opportunities.

qa_highlights.question: How much is outstanding from the Assam government on incentives?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR130 crore outstanding; total scheme value INR794 crore, now paid over 12 years, reducing FY27 expected receipts to about INR115 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a Northeast market share or competition concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no market share loss and that the Q1 dip reflects elections and monsoon, not Dalmia's capacity ramp.

risks_watch: Assam flooding and monsoon: July cement volumes fell about 12% YoY, Q2 volume growth expected to stay muted, and recovery depends on September catch-up and H2 double-digit growth.

Fuel and packing cost path: fuel guided down from INR1.55 in Q1 to about INR1.45 in Q2, but dependent on FSA rake availability; PP bag costs tied to crude and the international war situation, which management called hard to predict.

Assam incentive receipts: about INR130 crore outstanding; FY27 incentive revised to about INR115 crore from INR145 crore under the new equated payout over 12 years, with the subsidy drag expected to end after September 2026.

Rajasthan (Nimbol) and Haryana (Jhajjar) execution: EC expected around early October, groundwork from mid-October to November, commissioning in 18-20 months; capex quantum still being finalised (plus or minus INR100-200 crore).

West Bengal grinding decision pending the state industrial policy (around 15 August): Siliguri brownfield versus the 2 million tonne Begusarai (Bihar) grinding plan, with a decision promised on the next investor call.
Building Solutions (AAC/RMC) revenue target of INR150 crore: current run-rate is below it, with ARR expected to reach that level only by Q4 FY27.
key_quotes: So in Q2, as we all know, the Assam is completely flooded at the moment. So I don't see much of a stride in terms of volume in Q2.
I think INR1,500, INR1,600 is still a good estimate.
So I think the hit that the books are facing because of the subsidy will stop being felt after September onwards, and you'll start seeing a growth thereafter.

So we are not at the moment actively thinking of QIP. We will do it at the opportune time in case there's opportunities available for which we need to further raise money that may be organic or inorganic.
summary.management_tone: Management was cautious and somewhat defensive on Q1, calling it below expectations due to unforeseen global and state events, and guided Q2 to a similar trajectory. It was confident on the medium term, pointing to pent-up demand in H2, cost initiatives over 3-6 months, and the subsidy drag ending after September 2026, while leaving the West Bengal grinding and Rajasthan capex quantum open.
